lectures.title: Time and Space Complexity of Doubly Linked List

cues.en: All right.
In this lecture we are going to look at big picture of time and space complexity in double linked list.
The first operation is creating double linked list.
Now when we are creating an empty double linked list, this is not going to be the time consuming operation.
So the time and space complexity is going to be zero one, because here we are just declaring the head
and tail and length and setting head and tail to null and length to zero.
Then we have append method.
So with append method we are appending the element at the beginning of double linked list.
So here we are just updating the next and previous references and head.
So this is going to be a one time complexity.
Then we have prepend method.
So prepend method adds the element at the end of the double linked list.
So this is going to be the zero one time complexity.
And space complexity is zero one.
Now when it comes to the insert method we are specifying the index to be inserted.
So that's why we have to find out the node which is located before this index.
So in the worst case we have to loop through all nodes of the double linked list.
So that's why it's going to be on time complexity.
So here regardless of the size we are inserting one node.
That's why the space complexity is going to be all one, but the time complexity is o n because of the
traversal.
Now, when it comes to the search method, we know that it is using linear approach, and linear approach
takes on time complexity.
So here again the space complexity is O one.
Now traversal means that we are traversing the all elements of the double linked list.
So this is going to be on time complexity.
Similarly when we are doing the reverse traversal we are starting from the last node and visiting all
nodes until the first node.
So this is going to take all n time complexity.
Now when it comes to the get method in double linked list, we have a optimized version of the get method.
So this means that the time complexity is going to be o n divided by two.
But we know that in case of time complexity we can eliminate the constants.
So it's going to be on time complexity.
But the number of operations will be less.
And space complexity is going to be O one.
Now the set method also uses the Get method.
That is why the time complexity here also o n and the space is o one.
Now the pop first method removes the element from the beginning of the double linked list.
Here we are just updating the references.
So that's why the time and space complexity is o one.
Now when it comes to the pop method, it is removing the last element from the double linked list.
Now we know that in case of the single linked list, pop method takes on time complexity.
But in case of double linked list, it takes all one time complexity.
Because here we have the backward reference from the last node to the second last node.
That's why by using this we are updating the references easily without any loop.
So that's why the time complexity is O one.
And the space complexity is obviously that it's going to be O one.
Now, when it comes to the remove method, remove method takes index and finds the node and remove that
node.
So for finding the node we are going to use the get method.
And the get method takes on time complexity.
That's why it will affect the remove method also.
And the remove method takes o n time complexity.
So the space complexity is also o one.
Now when we are deleting the old nodes, we are not looping through the double linked list.
We are just updating the head and tail to point to null.
Then the garbage collector clears the nodes which are not referenced by root.
That's why the time complexity is going to be o one and the space complexity is O one.
Now this is the big picture of time and space complexity of double linked list.
So hopefully everything is clear about all operations in double linked list.
